prerequisites: Solid knowledge of digital electronics acquired in any of the degrees that allow access to the Master's.
Knowledge related to microcontroller or microprocessor programming (recommended).

learning_outcomes.text: Design high-complexity digital circuits, from high-level VHDL languages.
Perform functional simulations of complex digital circuits using hardware description languages.
Perform the analysis and temporal simulation of complex digital circuits.
Generate the test of a high-complexity digital circuit, using different algorithms.
Select the appropriate programmable digital circuit for each application.
Design and implement communication circuits based on complex programmable devices.

syllabus_topics: Classes of programmable logic devices: PLDS, FPGAS, SEA-GATES
Functional simulation, temporal and fault analysis
Combinational and sequential circuits with VHDL
assessment_rules: To pass the theoretical block, a minimum of 4 points is required on the exam. To pass the practical block, a minimum of 5 points is required, calculated as 0.3*Pr1 + 0.15*Inf + 0.55*Pr2. If both minimums are met, the final grade is 0.35*Theoretical Block Grade + 0.65*Practical Block Grade. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. It is a necessary condition to have submitted and defended both projects (Pr1 and Pr2) at least one week before taking the theoretical exam.
